title: The Spectral Cost of Detecting Nonequilibrium at Finite Temporal Resolution
abstract: A detector that cannot take two snapshots closer than a time $τ_0$ still identifies a fully observed finite Markov generator exactly, provided its gaps are randomized by two clocks. Identification is not detection. For a normal nonequilibrium network, the number of snapshots needed to reject every hidden equilibrium explanation grows as $e^{2γ_{\mathrm{irr}}τ_0}$, where $γ_{\mathrm{irr}}$ is the slowest damping of rotating modes. No adaptive schedule beats this rate, and a test on one dependent trajectory attains it.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a fundamental, exponential lower bound on the number of measurements needed to detect non-equilibrium dynamics in a stochastic system. The cost scales exponentially with the minimum measurement time gap ($	au_0$) and is governed by the slowest damping rate ($\gamma_{	ext{irr}}$) of the system's irreversible modes. This result sets a rigorous benchmark for experimental detection limits in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
main_problem: Determining the minimum number of measurements required to statistically distinguish a true non-equilibrium stochastic process from any hidden equilibrium process, given a finite minimum measurement gap.
main_result: The required number of snapshots scales exponentially with the minimum measurement gap ($	au_0$), specifically $N^* \propto e^{2\gamma_{	ext{irr}}	au_0}$, where $\gamma_{	ext{irr}}$ is the slowest damping rate of the rotating modes.
method: The analysis uses information-theoretic bounds, relating detectability to relative entropy and causal stopping times, establishing both lower and upper bounds on the required sample size.
model_or_system: The study analyzes stochastic systems governed by finite Markov generators ($Q$), comparing the true irreversible dynamics against the null class of reversible Markov chains.
key_observables: Minimum expected number of snapshots ($N^*$), entropy production rate, and the measurable current ($V$).
important_parameters: Minimum measurement gap ($	au_0$), the slowest damping rate ($\gamma_{	ext{irr}}$), and the statistical significance level ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The process starts in stationarity, and the analysis holds for every causal timing strategy and prespecified measurement schedule.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the exponential scaling of the observation cost for a driven ring, showing the analytic lower bound matching the achievable upper bound, and demonstrating the robustness of the test against hidden equilibrium controls.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the core problem by comparing non-equilibrium vs. equilibrium dynamics. It derives the exponential lower bound using information theory and then shows that this bound is achievable by a fixed, non-adaptive measurement protocol.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental, quantitative limit on the experimental feasibility of detecting true non-equilibrium dynamics in physical systems, linking measurement limitations directly to the spectral properties ($\gamma_{	ext{irr}}$) of the underlying master equation.
